stem: Which choice does USDA MyPlate count in the Dairy Group?

options.A: Fortified soy milk or fortified soy yogurt
options.B: Butter because it is made from milk
options.C: Cream cheese because it is made from milk
options.D: Almond milk automatically, regardless of nutrient fortification

rationale: USDA MyPlate includes milk, yogurt, cheese, lactose-free milk, and fortified soy milk and yogurt in the Dairy Group. It specifically excludes foods such as butter and cream cheese that contain little calcium and high fat, and it does not classify other plant-based “milks” as Dairy Group foods merely because they contain calcium.
educational_objective: Identify foods that USDA MyPlate currently includes in the Dairy Group.
source_document_title: Dairy Group – One of the Five Food Groups
source_locator: What foods are included in the Dairy Group?; For those who choose not to eat or drink dairy products
source_claim_supported: Fortified soy milk and yogurt are included in the Dairy Group; butter and cream cheese are excluded, and other plant-based milks are not in the Dairy Group based solely on calcium content.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
correction_summary: Replaced the vague “balanced plate/proportions” wording with a precise current MyPlate classification that has a single official-page locator.
audit_findings: A is explicitly included by USDA. B and C are explicitly excluded examples; D overstates inclusion of other plant beverages. No second answer remains.
